newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - IRELAND - AUGUST 11.

text.p: Following are the highlights of the Irish press on Monday:
- Sinn Fein has urged the Ulster Unionists to participate in the all-party talks which start at Stormont Castle in Belfast next month.
- Marie Geoghegan-Quinn is expected to seek a Fianna Fail nomination to contest the presidency despite Albert Reynolds' declaration that he wants to be the party candidate.
- An offer of "qualified immunity" has been made by the Director of Public Prosecutions to the man involved in allegations over a cash payment to Foreign Affairs Minister Ray Burke.
- The take-home pay of the average Irish worker is higher than most European counterparts, including those in Germany, France and Britain, a new survey says.
- Fianna Fail backbenchers appear to favour SDLP leader John Hume over former prime minister Albert Reynolds as a candidate for president.
- Sinn Fein has a team of more than 40 people lined up for the inter-party talks due to start in Belfast on September 15.
- A new competition for a National Conference Centre is expected to be announced this week by the Minister for Tourism, Sport and Recreation Jim McDaid.
- Clare returned to their field of dreams yesterday as they battled to a second All-Ireland hurling final in three years.
- The strength of the Irish police force is to be increased to 12,000 with a major recruiting drive due to get underway in September.

- A leading member of the loyalist Progressive Unionist Party predicted last night that all political prisoners in Northern Ireland will be released if the cease-fires hold and a peace settlement is reached.
